questions.questionText: One reason why merit goods, such as education and health care, can lead to market failure is that
options: individuals are unwilling to pay for merit goods.
individuals have incomplete information about merit goods.
merit goods are generally provided free by the government.
merit goods are subject to the free-rider problem.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that the consumption of unhealthy foods can best be reduced through the use of nudges and other techniques from behavioural economics.
A government decides that visitor centres in nature reserves are merit goods and therefore increases their provision. It can be concluded that this decision
options: avoided government failure.
did not have an opportunity cost.
ensured provision of a public good.
involved a normative judgement.

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows the free market demand (D1) and supply (S) curves for a merit good. D2 is the demand curve if all the benefits from consuming the good are taken into account. Which one of the following government policies would be most likely to achieve the socially optimal level of consumption?
options: A maximum price of P3
A minimum price of P2
A subsidy of P1 minus P3 per unit
A subsidy of P2 minus P3 per unit

questions.questionText: Which one of the following government policies is most likely to reduce market failure and to improve the allocation of resources?
options: A higher rate of tax on all firms earning profit
A minimum price for demerit goods above their free market price
Free market pricing for the provision of public goods
Subsidies paid to all loss-making firms to maintain full employment

questions.questionText: Figure 3 shows the market demand (D1) and supply (S) of loft insulation material. If consumers have full information about the benefits of insulating their lofts, demand will be D2. There is underproduction, Q2 – Q1, of loft insulation material because
options: at the social optimum, Q2, the price would be too high.
firms have no incentive to increase output beyond Q1.
firms lack information about the external benefits of loft insulation.
the government has failed to set a minimum price for loft insulation.

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the free market supply (S) and demand (D1) for a good when there is imperfect information. D2 shows the level of demand if consumers had full information about the effects of consuming the good. Which one of the following government policies is most likely to result in the social optimum level of consumption?
options: A maximum price equal to P3
A minimum price equal to P2
A subsidy per unit equal to P1 – P2
A tax per unit equal to P3 – P2

questions.questionText: In the following diagram D1 shows the market demand for smoke alarms when consumers have imperfect information about the benefits of installing a smoke alarm. If consumers had full information, the market demand for smoke alarms would be D2. Which one of the following policies is most likely to ensure that consumption and production of smoke alarms are at the social optimum level?
options: A maximum price set at P0
A maximum price set at P2
A subsidy per unit equal to P1 – P0
A subsidy per unit equal to P2 – P0

questions.questionText: Which one of the following applies to merit goods?
options: Their marginal private benefit is greater than their marginal social benefit.
They are likely to be provided by the market.
They can only be supplied by the government.
They have the characteristics of non-excludability and non-rivalry.

questions.questionText: Demerit goods represent a type of market failure because
options: their consumption results in positive externalities.
their production results in negative production externalities.
they are over-consumed in a free market.
they are under-consumed when left to free market forces.

questions.questionText: Explain why, in a free market, sugary drinks may be overconsumed.
Evaluate the view that imposing a tax is the most effective government policy for reducing the market failures arising from overconsumption of unhealthy food and drink.

The diagram below shows the demand and supply curves for a good provided solely by a free market. Currently, output is at OQ1. However, there is a misallocation of resources resulting in market failure. The socially optimal level of production is OQ2. Which one of the following statements is correct? The diagram shows the market for
options: a merit good.
a public good.
a good with negative externalities in production.
a good with positive externalities in production.
